label: Next best task
prompt:
Continue working on this project. Follow CLAUDE.md. Before picking the next task, scan in order: (1) interrupted/uncommitted work to resume, (2) failing tests or broken flows, (3) SSOT/DRY/quality violations, (4) mission alignment. Pick whichever is highest user impact and execute it fully. No questions, no scope creep. When done, update the session file with exactly these lines:
done: <one sentence what you completed>
next: <one sentence what remains>
tests: <N pass · N fail, or 'no suite'>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Test & fix
prompt:
Run the full test suite and fix every failure. Then start the dev server and use browser automation to walk the primary user flows — find what is visually broken or functionally wrong and fix it. If all tests pass and flows work, write tests for the most critical untested paths. Follow CLAUDE.md throughout. When done, update the session file:
done: <what you fixed>
next: <what remains>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Commit & push
prompt:
Prepare and ship today's work. Step 1 — verify: run type check and any tests; they must pass. Step 2 — review: check git diff and git status; confirm only intended changes are staged. Step 3 — commit: write a conventional commit message (<type>(<scope>): <description>) that explains WHY, not just what. Step 4 — push to origin. Step 5 — if this is a Vercel project, monitor the deployment until it shows Ready. Report the final git log line and deployment URL. When done, update the session file:
done: committed and pushed — <commit message>
next: <next priority>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Code quality pass
prompt:
Code health pass. Run linter and type checker to zero warnings. Find and fix: DRY violations, SSOT gaps, magic numbers, hardcoded strings, copy-paste code, TODO debt. No new features — only raise the bar on existing code. Follow CLAUDE.md. When done, update the session file:
done: <what you cleaned up>
next: <remaining debt>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Full audit + plan
prompt:
Comprehensive audit: run tests, check types, count TODOs, list incomplete features, identify tech debt and architectural gaps. Write a priority list by user impact. Execute the single highest-priority item fully. Follow CLAUDE.md. No speculative work. When done, update the session file:
done: <what you fixed>
next: <top remaining item from your priority list>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Mission alignment
prompt:
Read CLAUDE.md and extract or infer the project mission: who is the user, what problem does this solve, what does success look like. If no mission is explicitly written, draft one in 2 sentences and prepend it to CLAUDE.md under a '## Mission' heading. Then audit the last 10 commits and current codebase: are we building the right things? Is anything over-engineered, gold-plated, or missing entirely? Fix the single biggest misalignment. When done, update the session file:
done: <what you realigned or defined>
next: <next misalignment to address>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Browser test
prompt:
Use the browser automation tools (mcp__playwright or mcp__claude-in-chrome) to test this application in a real browser. Navigate to the running dev server. Test all primary user flows one by one: open the app, verify it loads without errors, walk the critical paths (create, read, update, delete where applicable), check mobile viewport (375px width), and read the browser console for errors. Fix every bug you find. Report what passed, what was broken, and what you fixed. When done, update the session file:
done: <what you tested and fixed>
next: <remaining issues or untested flows>
tests: <flows tested / flows passing>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Deploy checklist
prompt:
Full pre-deploy verification. Run each check and report pass/fail: (1) Type check — zero errors (tsc --noEmit or equivalent), (2) Build — must complete without error (npm run build or equivalent), (3) Tests — all passing, (4) No console.log or debug code in production paths, (5) No hardcoded secrets, API keys, or credentials, (6) All user-facing API routes have input validation, (7) No incomplete features behind missing guards, (8) Check for obvious security issues (SQL injection, XSS, auth bypass). Fix every failure. Only when ALL checks pass: commit, push, and monitor deployment to completion. When done, update the session file:
done: <pre-deploy checks result + deployed if clean>
next: <any items that need attention post-deploy>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Product thinking
prompt:
Step back from the code and think as a product manager. Review what exists and ask: (1) Who is the actual user and what is their single biggest pain point right now? (2) What is the most confusing part of the current UX — would a new user understand it in 30 seconds? (3) What feature would have the highest impact if shipped this week? (4) Is there anything that should be cut — features that add complexity without proportional value? Produce a prioritized list of 5 product improvements with rationale. Then execute the single highest-impact UX fix. When done, update the session file:
done: <product insight + fix applied>
next: <next highest-impact improvement>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: UX / design review
prompt:
Review the UI/UX of this application as a demanding but fair user. Start the dev server and open the app in a browser. Systematically check: (1) Typography — is all text readable? Minimum 14px body, high contrast (no dark gray on dark bg), (2) Interactive elements — are buttons, links, and inputs obviously clickable? (3) Mobile — does it work at 375px viewport width? (4) Empty states — what does the user see when there is no data? (5) Loading states — are async operations shown clearly? (6) Error states — are errors helpful and actionable? (7) Visual hierarchy — is the most important thing the most prominent thing? Report specific issues as file:line references and fix the top 3. When done, update the session file:
done: <UX issues found and fixed>
next: <remaining UX issues>
tests: flows passing
todos: <count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>

label: Marketing copy
prompt:
Review this project and write compelling marketing copy. Create all of the following: (1) One-line value proposition — under 12 words, outcome-focused, no jargon, (2) Three-sentence elevator pitch — what it does, who it's for, why it matters, (3) Three feature bullets — each written as a user benefit ('You can...' not 'It has...'), (4) One call-to-action line, (5) Three potential objections and how to answer them. Save the copy to MARKETING.md in the project root. Focus on the user's outcome, not the technology stack. When done, update the session file:
done: wrote marketing copy to MARKETING.md
next: review copy with fresh eyes, refine weakest section
tests: n/a
todos: 0
health: good

label: Social media content
prompt:
Based on what was built or improved in this project recently (check git log for the last week), write ready-to-post social media content: (1) Twitter/X post — under 280 chars, show something concrete (a feature, a metric, a before/after), include one relevant hashtag, (2) LinkedIn post — 3 paragraphs: the problem, what was built, what you learned. Conversational, no buzzwords, (3) A short demo script — 3 bullet points describing what to show in a 30-second screen recording. Keep it authentic — show the actual work, not generic hype. Save to SOCIAL.md in the project root. When done, update the session file:
done: wrote social content to SOCIAL.md
next: record demo video using the script
tests: n/a
todos: 0
health: good

label: Close session
prompt:
Close this work session cleanly so the next session can start cold. Perform these steps in order:

Step 1 — Finish uncommitted work:
Run git status. If there are uncommitted changes, commit them with a conventional commit message (<type>(<scope>): <description>). If scratch/debug work, stash or discard it.

Step 2 — Quality gate:
Run the project type checker and linter (e.g. tsc --noEmit && eslint src/ for TypeScript). They must pass with zero errors. Fix any failures before continuing.

Step 3 — Run tests:
Run the project test suite. Note the result (N pass / N fail).

Step 4 — Write session handoff:
Determine the tab name: run `grep -i "$(pwd -P)" ~/.config/claude-projects.conf | head -1 | cut -d'|' -f1 | tr -d ' '`. Use that as TAB (fall back to directory name if empty). Write exactly these lines to ~/.claude/sessions/<TAB>.md:
done: <one sentence — what was completed this session>
next: <one sentence — the single most important action for next session>
tests: <e.g. "18/18 smoke pass · tsc clean · eslint clean">
todos: <e.g. "0 TODOs">
health: <good | degraded | critical> — HEAD <short-git-hash>, <one-line status>

Step 5 — Final report:
Print a clear summary:
- Uncommitted changes: YES (committed as <hash>) / NO / STASHED
- Quality checks: PASS / FAIL
- Tests: PASS (N/N) / FAIL
- Session file written to: ~/.claude/sessions/<TAB>.md
- Safe to close this tab: YES / NO — <reason if NO>

(Note: the popup-suppression sentinel is written automatically by the infrastructure — you do not need to write any /tmp files.)

label: Continue
prompt: Resolve the pending question using available context and keep going. Follow CLAUDE.md. Do not stop to ask again. When done, update the session file with done/next/tests/todos/health lines.
